title: Continuous prepared-solve response-space damping path equivalence
question: Can the G19 lambda=1 -> 1/2 -> 1/4 affine-response damping sequence be traversed inside one continuously evolving live F-GC38 MODFLOW prepared solve, with fixed XOLD and no direct X control, while each settled response state remains numerically equivalent to its G19 fresh-origin reference and preserves the frozen SWAP status topology?

separation.research_subject: Prepared-solve transport/path equivalence of an already-qualified bounded response-space bridge.
not_claimed: That response-space damping is identical to head-space P4 outside the G19 affine case.
That one MODFLOW solve iteration per lambda is sufficient for coupling globalization.
That the final prepared solve is an accepted/published MODFLOW timestep.
That E3 or response-space damping is production policy.

prepared_solve_protocol: Initialize one live MODFLOW kernel from the frozen G11 groundwater model and call prepare_time_step once.
Acquire and open exactly one Modflow6PreparedSolveSession; capture accepted XOLD.
For lambda=1, publish the corresponding G19 affine response repeatedly in the same prepared solve until MODFLOW first reports convergence; record the current X head.
Without finalizing, resetting, restoring or directly mutating X, switch the published response to lambda=1/2 and continue the same prepared solve until first reported convergence.
At every solve iteration require accepted XOLD to remain bitwise identical to the captured origin.
After each settled lambda state, obtain one real-SWAP G16 diagnostic observation at the MODFLOW head and require no accepted-state/ledger/candidate authority.
After lambda=1/4, finalize_solve exactly once but do not call finalize_time_step. Kernel teardown is test cleanup, not timestep acceptance.
gates: Exactly one prepare_solve and one prepared-solve session for all three lambdas.
XOLD bitwise unchanged for every external nonlinear iteration.
No direct mutation or restore of X/XOLD and no session invalidation.
Each lambda reaches a MODFLOW convergence flag before switching to the next response.

Prepared-solve settled head for each lambda agrees with the corresponding G19 fresh-origin head within sqrt(machine epsilon float64) * max(1 m, absolute head scale), the existing F-GC38 nonlinear-path equivalence guard.
The SWAP status topology at the prepared-solve settled heads is exactly [6,6,0] for lambda [1,1/2,1/4].
All SWAP checks use G16 diagnostic observations and leave revision/time/ledger unchanged with no live candidate.
Exactly one finalize_solve and zero finalize_time_step calls.
pass_interpretation: PASS qualifies the bounded numerical/ownership fact that the G19 response-space sequence can steer one continuous F-GC38 prepared solve through states equivalent, at the existing F-GC38 path-equivalence scale, to the G19 fresh-origin response solutions without groundwater state rollback. It does not yet qualify an outer coupling algorithm or production globalization policy.
fail_interpretation: Preserve the failure. Do not relax the F-GC38 path-equivalence guard, G19 lambda sequence, G11 groundwater model, SWAP status topology or continuous-X ownership semantics retrospectively.
